paragraphs.source_en: “My dear, it is already seven o'clock,” the master's wife called to him through the sliding paper door. “Do get up.” Whether the master was already awake or still asleep I do not know; he lay with his back turned inward and made no reply. Not answering is an old failing of my master's. When he is driven to the last extremity and must open his mouth to answer, he says only, “Mm.” Even that “Mm” is by no means easily brought forth. When a man becomes so indolent that even answering is a nuisance to him, there may be, in some respect, a certain charm about him. But he, of all men, has never once been loved by a woman. To speak of the matter before our eyes, even the wife destined to grow old with him seems not to value him very highly; so it would hardly be wrong to say that one may infer the rest. Abandoned by parents and brothers, he has naturally never received the fond attentions of some unrelated courtesan either. Nor is that all: even with his own wife he is scarcely popular. It follows still more surely that the ordinary ladies of the world would find him displeasing. Strictly speaking, I have no need to expose here the fact that my master is exceptionally unpopular with the opposite sex; but he himself has got the matter entirely wrong and insists on finding reasons for it, supposing that his wife's dislike of him is wholly due to the ill luck of his current year, and this notion has become the root of his troubles. Out of kindness, and in the hope of helping him to see himself clearly, I mention it here in passing.

paragraphs.source_en: No matter how his wife reminded him, when the time fixed by the policeman had come, the master paid no attention at all and did not even say “Mm”; plainly, then, the fault lay with the master and not with his wife. Having reached this conclusion, the master's wife assumed an air of, “If you are late, it is no affair of mine,” shouldered broom and duster, and went off to clean the study. Presently there came from the study a pattering sound of beating and thumping, which showed that, as usual, the customary cleaning had begun. Whether the purpose of cleaning is exercise or play is no concern of mine, since I am not charged with the duty of cleaning; I need only take no notice of it. Still, when it comes to the master's wife's method of cleaning rooms, one cannot help saying that it is utterly meaningless. Why do I say it is meaningless? Because this good wife cleans merely for the sake of cleaning. She taps the duster over the paper doors and runs the broom once across the mats. Thereupon the cleaning is complete. As for why she cleans, and what effect the cleaning has, she assumes not so much as a speck of responsibility. For that very reason, the clean places are clean every day, while the places where rubbish lies and dust has gathered remain forever heaped with rubbish and thick with dust. There is, after all, the old story of the sacrificial sheep for the monthly announcement, so doing a little cleaning may be better than doing none; yet even when she cleans, it is not really for my master's sake, and the fact that she takes the trouble to do it every day all the same is precisely where the master's wife's greatness lies. The relation between the wife and housecleaning is merely the product of many years of habit: a mechanical association has formed, binding the two firmly together. Nevertheless, as to the actual effect of the cleaning, it is just as it was before the master's wife was born, just as in the ancient days before dusters and brooms had been invented: it has not the slightest practical result. It seems that the relation of these two is like that between a proposition and its terms in formal logic: regardless of content, they are bound together.

paragraphs.source_zh: 不管妻子怎样提醒，警察规定的时间到了，主人根本不理，连“嗯”一声都没有，那么显然是主人没理，而决不是妻子。主人的妻子做了这样判断之后，便表现出“你去晚了，我可管不着”的架势，扛起笤帚和掸子到书斋里打扫去了。随后就在书斋里响起了啪嗒啪嗒敲打的声音，这说明又开始了那例行公事般的打扫工作。说起来，打扫的目的是在于运动呢还是在于游戏，由于我不担负打扫的任务，与我无关，所以我只要不闻不问就行了。不过说到主人的妻子打扫房间的方法，不能不说那是毫无意义的。为什么说它毫无意义呢？因为这位主人的妻子只是为打扫而打扫。掸子在纸拉门上敲一通，笤帚在铺席上过一遍。然后就打扫完成了。至于为什么要打扫，打扫的效果如何，她连芝麻大的责任都不负的。正因为如此，清洁的地方倒是每天都清洁，而有垃圾的地方、尘土积聚的地方，则永远堆积着垃圾和厚厚的尘土。曾经有个故事叫“告朔饩羊”嘛，这说明搞点打扫总比不打扫好，但是，即使打扫了，其实并不是为我家主人打扫的，但偏偏每天还要不辞辛劳地打扫一通，这正是主人的妻子伟大之处。妻子和打扫房间的关系，只是多年习惯的产物，形成机械式的联想，两者牢牢地联结在一起。尽管如此，至于打扫的实际效果，正和主人的妻子还未出生之前一样，正和掸子、笤帚还未发明出来之前的古昔一样，丝毫无实效可言。看来，这两者的关系，正如形式逻辑学中的命题与语词一样，不管其内容如何，是彼此结合在一起的。
